items.title: ‘Attack on press freedom’: Press Club of India condemns FIR against Maktoob Media
items.summary: The Press Club of India (PCI) has condemned the West Bengal Police’s decision to file an FIR against Maktoob Media over its reporting on the alleged exclusion of Muslim IAS and IPS officers from meetings during Union Home Minister Amit Shah's visits to the state. In a statement dated September 26, the PCI called the FIR “an attack on press freedom and part of the pattern to attempt to stop any independent journalism in the country.” The Press Club of India condemns the West Bengal Police's decision to file an FIR against Maktoob Media for its reporting. We urge the West Bengal Police to withdraw this FIR immediately and ensure that journalists are able to do their job without fear. @WBPolice pic.twitter.com/Ah0Q10JzZ6 — Press Club of India (@PCITweets) September 26, 2026 The FIR concerns a social media post relating to allegations first made public by Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra that senior Muslim officers were sidelined from official meetings because of their religion. According to the PCI, these allegations have been reported widely, but there has “been no official denial” from authorities, yet the police went ahead and filed the case regardless. According to The Wire , the case was registered at Bidhannagar Cyber Crime Police Station on September 19, following a written complaint by Saurav Banerjee, and cites posts on X and YouTube from Maktoob’s official channels. Although the case names an ‘UnknownPerson 1’, its contents refer directly to Maktoob’s social media posts and invoke several sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita concerning alleged promotion of enmity, outrage of religious feelings, statements causing public mischief, and defamation. Maktoob has said it was not informed by the police of the FIR and only learnt of it through a communication from X, which stated that the police had sought account creation, login and Android device details for the handle @MaktoobMedia. In its statement, the PCI argued that reporting serious allegations of this nature is journalism’s job, and that targeting Maktoob for doing so “cannot be justified”, particularly since independent constitutional authorities have themselves taken cognisance of the claims. items.title: Judiciary committed to protecting students' right to protest: CJI Surya Kant at CNLU Patna open house
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Saturday held an open house dialogue with students at Chanakya National Law University (CNLU), Patna. According to a press release issued by the University, the initiative was taken by the students, who invited the CJI to have a direct conversation with them. The session was organised by the University's Academic and Debating Committee and Legal Aid Cell. Responding to a student's question on the police response to peaceful protests, the CJI said that the judiciary remains committed to protecting students' fundamental right to peaceful protest. On financial difficulties faced by first-generation lawyers, the CJI referred to the Sarika Tyagi case, in which the Supreme Court had backed the setting up of a Young Lawyers' Professional Assistance Fund. He said that such support should be seen as a structural necessity for the profession's future and not charity. He also told students that concerns over skyrocketing tuition fees and inadequate scholarships would be addressed. CNLU Vice-Chancellor Prof Faizan Mustafa proposed shortening the five-year law degree to four years, with the final year as a mandatory court apprenticeship to eliminate the separate one-year practice requirement for judicial service exams. The CJI called it "a new, welcome idea." When asked why dissenting opinions within the Collegium are recorded but not made public, the CJI said that full disclosure could place individual judges in an untenable position and added that transparency has limits where personal dignity is concerned. Patna High Court Chief Justice V Kameswar Rao , who attended in his capacity as CNLU Chancellor, said that judicial clerkships at High Courts need to be made more competitive and better paid to compete with corporate law options.

items.title: CMRL Exalogic case: ED tells Kerala High Court police bound to register FIR against ex-CM Pinarayi Vijayan
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Saturday said that it would examine whether the State Police can conduct a preliminary enquiry into information given by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) on the CMRL-Exalogic case, before it decides whether to register a First Information Report (FIR) in the matter [ Adv KM Shajahan v State of Kerala & ors ]. The CMRL-Exalogic case involves allegations of corruption against former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and his daughter T Veena. A petition has been filed before the Kerala High Court by advocate KM Shajahan questioning why no FIR has yet been filed in the matter. The plea is tied to material allegedly shared by the ED with the Kerala police, following the ED's investigation into financial transactions between Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) and Exalogic Solutions Private Limited, a company owned by T Veena, the daughter of former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan. However, instead of registering an FIR, the State constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by Crime Branch Additional Director General of Police H Venkatesh, to conduct a preliminary enquiry. Shajahan's plea questions this move. His plea states that the ED has unearthed material indicating the possible commission of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (PC Act) and Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA), against Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter and former minister PA Muhammed Riyas. The ED, today supported Shajahan's plea for the registration of an FIR in the case. "My respectful submission is it has to be registered, my lord. That is no other option," the ED's counsel told the Court. Justice A Badharudeen , in turn, noted that the matter raises an important legal question as to whether a State agency had any discretion to decide whether or not to register an FIR in such matters. " While hearing, a pertinent legal question was raised for consideration as to whether, when information under Section 66(2) of the PMLA Act has been passed by the Enforcement Directorate to the State Police for registering FIR for the scheduled offences found during investigation, whether the State Police has any other option other than registering the FIR, or whether the State Police still has the option to go for a preliminary inquiry before registering the FIR. items.title: Punjab and Haryana High Court calls for aggressive measures to tackle Gurugram water crisis
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court recently took a serious note of the depletion of groundwater levels in Gurugram [ Sunil Singh v Ministry of Environment & Forests and Others ]. A Bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor said that the city was witnessing a water crisis due to the non-availability of potable water, and severe waterlogging during monsoons. It called for aggressive measures to improve the situation in Haryana's financial capital. "Unless appropriate and effective measures are pursued aggressively, the situation is likely to remain grim, particularly as continued urbanization and population growth appear inevitable, given Gurugram’s proximity to the National Capital," the Court said in an order passed on September 22. Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor The Court was hearing a case related to the preservation of groundwater levels in the municipal limits of Gurugram. It observed that Gurugram has been facing a persistent water crisis due to the non-availability of potable water. It noted that the indiscriminate use of borewells has resulted in a continuous depletion of groundwater levels over severe decades. "Further, the existing natural water bodies have substantially diminished, while the channels that sustained these water bodies remain largely blocked," the Bench said. While the city has been facing severe waterlogging during the monsoon, the rainwater so accumulated is not being effectively utilized for the purpose of replenishing the depleting groundwater level, the Court added. There is also an issue with regard to proper utilization of treated water with the effective utilization of sewage treatment plants, the Bench said. The Court has now asked the parties appearing in the matter to submit written suggestions regarding the remedial measures required to be undertaken in the matter and listed the matter for hearing on October 1 to hear the authorities posted in Gurugram. The Deputy Commissioner has been directed to join the hearing through video conferencing along with the heads of relevant departments. The Chief Engineer, Municipal Corporation, Gurugram, and the officers-in-charge of the Haryana Shehri Vikas Pradhikaran and Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority, shall also remain present through Video Conferencing on the date fixed, the Court directed. items.title: Madras High Court dismisses MGR heirs’ bid to revive decades-old estate dispute
items.summary: The Madras High Court has rejected an attempt by the legal heirs of former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MG Ramachandran’s brother to revive a claim over property forming part of the late actor-politician’s Sathya Gardens estate [ MC Ramamurthy Vs M Rajendran ]. Justice AD Maria Clete held that the property in question was covered by MGR’s Will of January 18, 1987, which had already been probated by the High Court in 1992. The Court, therefore, found untenable the heirs’ case that MGR had died intestate in respect of the property. Opening its order with a tribute to MGR, Justice Clete described him as one of Tamil Nadu’s “most distinguished personalities” who held an enduring place in the hearts of millions and dominated cinema and public life for nearly half a century. “ Though he passed away about four decades ago, his name and legacy remain vibrant in public memory .” Justice AD Maria Clete The dispute arose from an original petition filed in 2012 by persons claiming through MGR’s brother, MG Chakrapani. They sought Letters of Administration over property at Virugambakkam, contending that it was not covered by MGR’s Will and, consequently, would devolve upon them as his Class II legal heirs under the Hindu Succession Act. downloaded downloaded However, the administrator of MGR’s estate maintained that the property formed part of “Sathya Garden” referred to in the Will and had vested in the MGR School and Home for the Speech and Hearing Impaired Trust. The Court noted that the inventory placed before it specifically referred to Survey No. 255 of Virugambakkam Village, the survey number of the property involved in the present case. The Court said these materials established that the property had been included in the probated Will and administered as part of MGR’s estate. “ The very foundation of the original petition—that the late Dr M.G. Ramachandran died intestate in respect of the petition-schedule property —is demonstrably untenable," the Court ruled. It added that so long as the earlier testamentary grant continued to operate, another Letters of Administration proceeding could not be maintained on the footing that MGR had died intestate in respect of the same property. The Court also expressed serious concern over the manner in which the proceedings had been handled. items.title: No Muslim personal law immunity from POCSO case for sex with minor wife: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that a marriage recognised under Muslim personal law does not confer a man entering such a marriage immunity from criminal prosecution for having sexual intercourse with a wife under 18 years [ Bilal & Anr v The State Govt of NCT of Delhi through SHO & Ors ]. Justice Sanjeev Narula ruled that personal law cannot override the protections guaranteed under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act) and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS). “…a marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot, by reason of that status alone, confer immunity from POCSO or the BNS for sexual intercourse with a wife who was below eighteen at the relevant time. Any other view would create, through judicial decision, an exception which Parliament has expressly excluded,” the Court held. Justice Sanjeev Narula Delhi High Court Marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot confer immunity from POCSO or BNS for sexual intercourse with a wife who was below eighteen The Court made the observation while refusing to quash an criminal case registered against a man under Section 64(1) of the BNS and Section 6 of the POCSO Act. The man and his wife filed the plea had filed the plea, in which they also sought action against a police official and compensation for harassment. It was stated that they married when the woman was 16 years and three months old, and the man was 28. They subsequently lived together, and the woman became pregnant. Her age came to light when she visited a government hospital during her pregnancy. The woman maintained that the marriage had taken place voluntarily, with the consent of both families, and that she had not been subjected to force or coercion. She also supported the man's bail application and sought his presence during her pregnancy. In their plea, the couple argued that under Muslim personal law, a Muslim girl who had attained puberty was competent to marry and that the validity of the marriage meant that the subsequent sexual relationship could not attract criminal liability. However, the High Court drew a distinction between the civil validity of a marriage and the criminal consequences of sexual intercourse with a minor. It held that even if the marriage was assumed to be valid under Muslim personal law, that could not create an exception to POCSO or the BNS. items.title: Supreme Court stays proceedings in BJP MLA Bhupendra Singh’s suit against defamatory social media posts
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday stayed further proceedings in a defamation suit filed by BJP MLA and former Madhya Pradesh minister Bhupendra Singh over social media posts and videos that allegedly linked him to multiple murders and the illicit liquor trade [ Ravindra Jain v. Bhupendra Singh and Others ]. Singh had filed the suit before the Delhi High Court against Ravindra Jain, who runs the Bhopal-based Sabki Khabar YouTube channel, and several others. He alleged that Jain’s videos suggested that he was involved in the illicit liquor trade and linked him to several deaths in Madhya Pradesh. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta yesterday issued notice on Jain’s petition seeking the transfer of the suit from the Delhi High Court to a competent court in Bhopal. “ Let notice be issued to the remaining respondents. In the meantime, further proceedings in CS(OS) No.479 of 2026, titled ‘Bhupendra Singh v. Abhishek Jain & Ors.’ pending before the High Court of Delhi, shall remain stayed, ” the Court ordered. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta In May, the Delhi High Court had passed an interim order directing the removal of specified videos and social media posts. It also restrained certain defendants, including Jain, from publishing similar allegations while the suit remained pending. Jain subsequently approached the Supreme Court seeking the transfer of the suit to a competent court in Bhopal. Before the Supreme Court, Jain argued that Singh, the contesting defendants and the events discussed in the publications were all connected to Madhya Pradesh. He disputed Singh’s grounds for instituting the suit in Delhi and contended that the High Court had passed its interim order before giving him an opportunity to be heard. The top court has now issued notice on Jain’s transfer petition while staying further proceedings before the Delhi High Court. Advocate Shambhavi Shrivastava appeared for Jain. His plea was filed through Advocate Brajesh Pandey. Senior Advocate Siddharth Bhatnagar with Advocates Mukesh Kumar and Vedarth Shivhare, appeared for the respondents. [Read Order]

items.title: SIR voters need not attend hearings in most cases, says poll panel
items.summary: Amid reports of growing differences between Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, the Election Commission of India (ECI) on Saturday, September 26, announced a series of measures to ease the process for voters. The full Commission, comprising Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi, met at the ECI headquarters in New Delhi on Saturday. It announced that voters who have received SIR notices for being “unmapped” or having logical discrepancies will generally not have to appear before election officials. Instead, Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will visit their homes to collect documents and upload them on the ECINET system. The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) will then decide the matter based on the documents, the Commission said. The move comes as the poll panel faces mounting scrutiny over the SIR exercise and reports of disagreements among its members. The Indian Express has reported that Sandhu and Joshi had raised objections on several occasions over decisions and orders relating to SIR. The ECI has maintained that differences of opinion and observations are part of institutional deliberations. In Saturday’s press note, it also sought to emphasise that the SIR decisions were taken with the unanimous approval of the full Commission. SIR hearings to be held only in exceptional cases Under the new arrangement, voters who receive notices during SIR will not ordinarily be required to appear at the office of the ERO or Assistant ERO. Hearings will be held only in exceptional circumstances, as decided by the ERO, and will preferably be conducted online, the ECI said. If a hearing is required, an elector can authorise any adult member of their family to appear on their behalf. The Commission said facilities for online hearings would also be strengthened. District Election Officers (DEOs) have been directed to establish help desks and hold special camps, depending on local requirements, for people living in night shelters, labourers, poor people and homeless persons. ECI stresses SIR orders were unanimous The Commission's press note repeatedly emphasised that the SIR exercise had been approved unanimously. It said the June 24, 2025 order initiating SIR across all states and union territories, beginning with Bihar and followed by West Bengal and 30 other states and UTs, was approved unanimously. Amid allegations of autocratic decision-making within the Election Commission against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, retired Administrative Service (IAS) officer and former Kerala Chief Secretary Jiji Thomson has claimed in an interview with OnManorama that Gyanesh Kumar had previously persuaded him to contest a BJP election candidacy. The alleged offer was made in 2016, when Gyanesh Kumar was in service. Jiji Thomson stated that the conversation took place in 2016 on a flight to Delhi while he was still serving as Kerala’s Chief Secretary. He also clarified that he had declined the offer. Jiji Thomson is a retired 1980-batch IAS officer of the Kerala cadre who served as the Chief Secretary of Kerala in 2015-16 in the Oommen Chandy-led Congress government. “We had a good friendship. He told OnManorama that Gyanesh Kumar was very persuasive. “I declined it promptly,” he said. Jiji Thomson also said that Gyanesh Kumar was highly vocal and open about his support for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's growing popularity in Kerala. He said that, even after he declined the BJP seat, Gyanesh further tried to persuade him to enter politics. items.summary: Twenty three of the 31 films which were denied approval for screening at the International Documentary and Short Film Festival of Kerala have now been given censor exemption by the Union Ministry of Information & Broadcasting. However eight more films still await permission. Among these are five competition films, including the short fiction In Search of Buddha , long documentaries Redlight to Limelight and Parliament Street , and short documentaries The Mali and the Parasite and Sanitised Republic . Two long documentaries which are in focus category - Shimmering Odyssey and Far From Home - are also awaiting approval for screening. The 18th edition of the IDSFFK began on September 25, and initially the Union Ministry had disallowed the screening of 31 films which included a Malayalam film. However, after the government of Kerala wrote seeking permission to screen all the 31films, the Union Ministry approved 24 films, including a film that is in the waiting list of the festival. Although reasons for denying permission for the films have not been given, it is understood that the Ministry had taken issue with using Prime Minister Narendra Modi's voice over in the documentary Sanitised Republic . The filmmakers have edited the film twice after this to remove the reference of the Prime Minister's Office. The film focuses on sanitation workers who risked their lives during the COVID-19 pandemic but later lost their jobs in June 2022. Through their stories of struggle the film examines the enduring link between caste and sanitation work in India. Among the other films yet to get approval, In Search of Buddha traces the story of a forgotten Naxal leader called Buddha. Redlight to Limelight follows the mothers and children of a Kolkata brothel community and Parliament Street explores Delhi's Parliament Street through its landmarks, people and everyday spaces. Justice V Lakshminarayanan passed the order on Friday, September 25, while hearing a petition filed by Tulir Charitable Trust, which works on the prevention and healing of child sexual abuse. The court also directed the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case to issue a press release every week on the progress of the investigation. The John Doe order covers unnamed media organisations, social media accounts, and other entities, besides the respondents named in the petition. The court also directed anyone who had already uploaded material connected to the case to remove it by September 26 and ordered the police to take steps to ensure its removal, if necessary. A compliance report is to be filed at the next hearing. However, the court did not impose a blanket restriction on discussions about child abuse. It said media outlets and other entities could discuss issues arising from child abuse, as long as the discussions did not touch upon the factual matrix of the crime. items.title: 5 festive credit traps to avoid this festive season
items.summary: Festive offers are already landing. Zero-interest EMIs on phones, pre-approved limit increases, instant loans cleared in minutes. Most of it is genuinely useful. But several of these offers carry costs that do not appear on the price tag and only surface on your credit report months later, usually in January, when the bills arrive together. Five traps worth knowing before you shop. 1. A no-cost EMI blocks your credit limit for the entire tenure This is the one almost nobody checks, and it damages your score without you missing a single payment. When you take a no-cost EMI on a credit card, the full purchase value is blocked against your limit for the whole tenure. Buy a ₹60,000 phone on a ₹1 lakh card and ₹60,000 of that limit stays locked for nine months, even though you are repaying in instalments. Credit utilisation, the share of your limit you are using, is one of the largest single inputs into how bureaus calculate your score, commonly put at around 30%. Sitting at 60% utilisation for nine months pulls your score down for all nine of them. "You can pay every instalment perfectly and still watch your score fall," said Utkrishta Kumar, founder and chief executive of Oolka. "People assume a score only drops when you miss something. Utilisation does it quietly, in the background, while you are doing everything right." What to do: spread festive purchases across more than one card, or ask your issuer for a limit increase before you buy rather than after. 2. "No cost" does not mean no cost The interest on a no-cost EMI has not been waived. It has been repackaged. Three costs typically survive. GST at 18% on the interest component , which the retailer's discount does not cover and which you pay. A processing fee of 1% to 3% , plus GST on that fee, charged at the bank's discretion. And the discount you gave up , because the interest is usually funded by the cash discount or cashback you would otherwise have received. On a ₹30,000 phone with roughly ₹4,500 of embedded interest, the GST alone adds about ₹810. With a processing fee, that ₹30,000 purchase lands closer to ₹30,810 at minimum. What to do: ask for the upfront-payment price and the EMI price separately. Where a cash discount exists, paying upfront is usually cheaper. 3. items.title: How Delaying a Step-Up SIP Can Affect Your Long-Term Corpus
items.summary: A Step-Up SIP allows investors to increase their SIP contribution periodically as their income and financial capacity grow. Starting the increase earlier can give the additional investments more time to participate in market-linked growth. Delaying the step-up may therefore reduce the potential corpus, even when the total investment period remains unchanged. What Is a Step-Up SIP? A Step-Up SIP is a facility that enables an investor to increase the amount invested through a Systematic Investment Plan at predefined intervals. The increase may be structured as a fixed amount or a specified percentage of the existing SIP contribution. It allows investors to progressively increase their investments over time in line with changes in income, cash flows or financial goals, while continuing with a systematic investment approach. How Does Delaying a Step-Up SIP Affect the Corpus? When an investor postpones increasing their SIP, they continue investing the existing SIP amount for a longer period. The additional amount that could have been invested through a higher SIP therefore enters the portfolio at a later stage. For example, an investor may be investing ₹10,000 every month and later decide to increase the SIP to ₹12,000. If the investor postpones this increase for two years, the SIP continues at ₹10,000 during that period. The additional ₹2,000 per month starts getting invested only after the investor increases the SIP. The Timing of Higher Contributions Matters The impact of delaying the increase is not limited to the additional amount invested later. The timing of those additional investments also matters. An amount invested earlier has a longer period to potentially grow and compound, subject to market performance. As a result, continuing with the lower SIP for longer and increasing it at a later stage can lead to a different long term corpus compared with increasing the SIP earlier. The difference will depend on the amount of the increase, the length of the delay, the remaining SIP investment period and the returns generated during the respective periods. Factors to Consider When Reviewing a Delayed Step-Up SIP Whether an investor should increase the SIP after a period of delay depends on their current financial circumstances. Changes in the future financial requirement and investment capacity can both be relevant when reviewing the SIP amount. items.title: Commodity trading in India: why active traders are consolidating to one app
items.summary: Something unusual is happening at the edges of India's broking industry. Most of the largest platforms have struggled to add active users this year. A cluster of smaller, product-led brokers has been growing at a pace the incumbents cannot match. The obvious explanation, cheaper brokerage, is also the wrong one. Discount pricing has been the industry default for the better part of a decade. Why active traders keep a second account The real shift is about consolidation. Ask an active trader how many broking apps sit on their phone, and the honest answer is usually two or three. One for equity and F&O. Another for commodities. Sometimes a third for a chart or tool they cannot live without. Each account is a separate login, a separate ledger and a separate funding decision at nine in the morning. For years that friction was simply the cost of trading everything. It is now the thing traders are actively trying to remove. Sahi describes the pattern among its own users plainly: many came for options trading, stayed for the single-screen experience, and were waiting on commodities before they could close their other accounts. That wait ended in August, when commodities went live inside the Sahi app . "The last decade was really about accessibility and low cost, which we believe is now a solved problem," Dale Vaz, Sahi's co-founder and CEO, told The Economic Times this month. "As users become more familiar with the markets, they are looking for products and tools that help them make more informed decisions rather than just a buy-sell button." That framing explains the growth better than price does. When access is solved, competition moves up the stack: how fast an order fills, how much the screen tells you before you act, and how many markets you can reach without switching apps. On that measure the platform that wins is not the cheapest. It is the one that removes the most friction. Sahi as a case study Sahi is useful here precisely because it is young. The platform, operated by Aaritya Broking, launched publicly in December 2024. Its active client base rose 243% in 2026 to 2.53 lakh from 0.74 lakh at the start of the year, according to NSE data reported by The Economic Times, in a year when most of the biggest brokers were flat. items.title: Do Product Designers Need UI/UX Skills?
items.summary: Yes, and there isn't much room for debate here. Product design covers more ground than UI/UX design does on its own, but try doing the job without a working grasp of user experience and interface principles, and you'll run into trouble fast. A product can be backed by solid strategy and still fail if people find the interface confusing or the experience gets in their way. Most product designers end up touching pretty much the whole lifecycle of a product at some point. One week they are spotting a user problem, the next they are running research, then it's wireframes, interface design, testing prototypes, and eventually sitting down with developers to figure out how the thing actually gets built. UI/UX skills show up at nearly every one of these stages, even when the job title never actually says "UI/UX" on it. The more useful question isn't whether UI/UX matters. It's how much of it a given role actually requires, and whether product design and UI/UX design are really two names for the same job. That depends on the company. What tends to hold regardless is that designers with a foundation in both areas are better equipped to judge a product from the user's side of the screen, not just from how it looks in a file. What Is Product Design? Product design is mainly about building something that is able to solve a real user problem while still making sense for the business behind it. The process moves through several stages usually, though in practice these overlap way more than any list would suggest: ● Identifying what users actually need ● Researching to confirm it ● Framing the problem in usable terms ● Mapping how users move through the product ● Building wireframes ● Developing prototypes ● Designing the interface ● Testing whether the solution holds up ● Working with developers to ship it ● Adjusting based on what comes back Visual design shows up fairly late in that list. A lot of the actual work happens before anyone opens a design tool. What Is UI/UX Design? UI is User Interface – what you see on the screen.
